new_claim.statement: For every original-coordinate split A=[[B,C],[C^T,D]], every admissible cap-one product input satisfies int |phi_Q| <= L(B, P_ker(B) Range(C)), where L is the supremum of the affine active-block Fourier L1 budget over compact finite-fragment unit-measure product indicators. Range(B)-affine terms are exactly removable by physical translations; if B is invertible the leakage subspace is zero.

premises: Original-coordinate split preserves independence between active and outside coordinate groups.
Triangle inequality and Tonelli applied only after retaining the whole active block.
For symmetric B, Range(B) is the orthogonal complement of ker(B), allowing exact completion by translation.

partner_result_applied.application: Convexity plus TV lower semicontinuity of the active-block Fourier L1 functional gives exact reduction of its worst-case value to whole compact finite-fragment product-indicator laws.

unresolved_implication: Derive from the global three-large-eigenvalue hypothesis an original-coordinate or grouped active mechanism with a universal bound on L(B,P_ker(B)Range(C)), or prove an aggregate equivalent without selecting a tiny reciprocal minor.
next_step: In the remaining singular/grouped branches, charge only kernel leakage and combine aggregate ridge/exterior-mass results before reciprocal inversion; never pay range-affine translations or individual fragment scales.
